result.topic_en: The page completes a spherical-trigonometric integration method: it reduces the differential to dφ = p dq/((1−qq)√(1−pp−qq)), gives a four-step complete solution, and discusses the criterion by which cot r drops out of the calculation.
result.transcription:
518 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Calc. integr.
Cum vero $\cot\xi = u\cot r - t = \frac{(1-qq)\cot r + pq}{\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}}$, erit
$\sin^2\xi = \frac{1-pp-qq}{(1-qq)(1-pp+2pq\cot r+(1-qq)\cot^2 r)}$
unde denique fit
$d\varphi = \frac{pdq}{(1-qq)\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}}$.
Ubi commode usu venit, ut solum differentiale $dq$ hic insit, alterum vero $dp$ una cum tangente $r$ ex calculo excesserit; hanc ob rem non $p$ per $q$ ita definiamus, ut haec formula ad arcum circuli reducatur, sed potius relationem inter quantitates $q$ et $\sin\varphi$ tanquam cognitam spectemus, quam adeo pro lubitu assumere licebit; tum igitur $\frac{d\varphi}{dq}$ erit quantitas algebraica et vocetur $\frac{d\varphi}{dq}=s$, atque ex aequatione $s=\frac{p}{(1-qq)\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}}$ determinemus quantitatem $p$; quia enim $\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}=\frac{p}{s(1-qq)}$ erit $1-pp-qq=\frac{pp}{ss(1-qq)^2}$, unde reperiri potest $p$ et sequens solutio completa concluditur:
1. Constituta relatione quacunque algebraica inter $\sin\varphi$ et $q$, positoque $\frac{d\varphi}{dq}=s$, quaeratur quantitas $p$ ex hac aequatione $\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}=\frac{p}{s(1-qq)}$.
2. Inventa hac quantitate $p$ sumatur $\tan r=\frac{dq}{dp}$, atque hinc porro
$u=\frac{1-qq}{\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}}$, $t=-\frac{pq}{\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}}=-sq(1-qq)$.
3. Deinde quaeratur arcus $y$, ut sit $\cos y = q\cos r - p\sin r$.
4. Hinc porro angulus $\xi$, ut sit $\cot\xi = u\cot r - t$, quo angulo invento habebimus $x=\xi+\varphi$, sicque problema expedite est solutum.
NB. Hic autem etiamnunc desideratur criterium, ex quo pateat in formula $d\varphi=(du\cot r - dt)\sin^2\xi$ quantitatem $\cot r$ ex calculo tolli; in hoc ipso enim vis methodi consistit, ut $r$ ex calculo excedat, propterea quod $\tan r$ per $dp$ et $dq$ determinatur. Ad hoc ergo criterium, ob
$\sin^2\xi=\frac{1}{1+tt-2tu\cot r+uu\cot^2 r}$
requiritur, ut ostendatur ex expressione
$d\varphi=\frac{du\cot r - dt}{uu\cot^2 r-2tu\cot r+1+tt}$
omnino tolli $\cot r$, propterea quod sit $\tan r=\frac{dq}{dp}$; hinc enim etiam ratio differentialium $dt$ et $du$ quantitatem $\cot r$ involvet, sed quomodo? Supra invenimus $u\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}=1-qq$, $(1+tt)(1-pp-qq)=(1-pp)(1-qq)$, $(1+tt)\sqrt{(1-pp-qq)}=u(1-pp)$, $\frac{1+tt}{u}=\frac{u(1-pp)}{1-qq}$, $\frac{(1+tt)(1-qq)}{uu}=1-pp$, $pp=1-\frac{(1+tt)(1-qq)}{uu}$,
$1-pp-qq=\frac{1+tt-qq(1+tt+uu)}{uu}$, $1+tt-qq(1+tt+uu)=1-2qq+q^4$, unde pro determinando $q$ haberetur haec aequatio
$q^4-qq(1-tt-uu)=tt$
Unde patet praestare loco $t$ et $u$ valores per $p$ et $q$ introducere, uti fecimus, ubi ob $dp=dq\cot r$ statim se prodidit criterium quaesitum.
Notatu etiam dignum est, quod prodeat $d\varphi=-\frac{tdq}{q(1-qq)}$, ubi jam neque $p$ neque $u$ inest, ita ut ex relatione $\frac{d\varphi}{dq}=s$ habeatur $t=-sq(1-qq)$.
A. m. T. I. p. 37 — 41.

items.quote: non $p$ per $q$ ita definiamus, ut haec formula ad arcum circuli reducatur, sed potius relationem inter quantitates $q$ et $\sin\varphi$ tanquam cognitam spectemus, quam adeo pro lubitu assumere licebit
items.english: Let us not define p in terms of q so that this formula reduces to a circular arc, but rather regard the relation between q and sin φ as known, which may then be assumed at will.
And thus the problem has been readily solved.

items.quote: Hic autem etiamnunc desideratur criterium, ex quo pateat in formula $d\varphi=(du\cot r - dt)\sin^2\xi$ quantitatem $\cot r$ ex calculo tolli
items.english: Here, however, a criterion is still wanting, from which it would be evident that in the formula dφ = (du cot r − dt) sin²ξ the quantity cot r is removed from the calculation.

items.quote: hinc enim etiam ratio differentialium $dt$ et $du$ quantitatem $\cot r$ involvet, sed quomodo?
items.english: For hence the ratio of the differentials dt and du will also involve the quantity cot r, but how?

items.quote: Unde patet praestare loco $t$ et $u$ valores per $p$ et $q$ introducere, uti fecimus, ubi ob $dp=dq\cot r$ statim se prodidit criterium quaesitum.
items.english: Hence it is clear that it is better to introduce, in place of t and u, their values in terms of p and q, as we did, where because dp = dq cot r the desired criterion revealed itself at once.

items.quote: Notatu etiam dignum est, quod prodeat $d\varphi=-\frac{tdq}{q(1-qq)}$, ubi jam neque $p$ neque $u$ inest, ita ut ex relatione $\frac{d\varphi}{dq}=s$ habeatur $t=-sq(1-qq)$.
items.english: It is also worth noting that dφ = −t dq/(q(1−qq)) results, in which neither p nor u appears, so that from the relation dφ/dq = s one has t = −sq(1−qq).
